title: Closed points meet locally closed subsets of a punctured local spectrum
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $U=X\setminus\{\mathfrak m\}$ with its subspace topology. For every nonempty locally closed subset $W\subseteq U$, there is a point $w\in W$ whose singleton $\{w\}$ is closed in $U$. Here local means that $\mathfrak m$ is the unique maximal ideal, and locally closed means the intersection of an open subset and a closed subset of $U$.

source.place: Tag 02J6, lemma-ubiquity-Jacobson-schemes, case (4); equivalently Properties Tag 02IM, lemma-complement-closed-point-Jacobson, case (1), using the locally-closed characterization immediately after Topology Tag 005U, definition-space-jacobson.

proof.text: The closed subsets of $X$ are the sets $V(I)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes]. Given a descending chain of closed sets, take their radical ideals; the radical formula in [lem-weil-pbc-zero-locus-eq-iff-radical-eq] turns it into an ascending chain of ideals. Its union is an ideal; its finite generators, supplied by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], all belong to one member, so the chain stabilizes. Thus $X$ is Noetherian as a topological space. The spectrum is Kolmogorov: by the closure formula in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], equality of the closures of two points gives inclusion of their primes in both directions, hence equality. Every subspace, in particular $W$, is Kolmogorov: intersect an ambient open separating two points with that subspace.

source.place: Tag 02IM, lemma-complement-closed-point-Jacobson, direct proof of (1): Noetherian and Kolmogorov hypotheses, expanded from definitions.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-noetherian-space-compact-subsets] to the affine scheme $X$ and its subset $W$: $W$ is quasi-compact with its subspace topology. Since $W$ is nonempty and Kolmogorov, [lem-sc-quasi-compact-kolmogorov-closed-point], with ambient space $W$ and closed subset all of $W$, supplies a point $w\in W$ whose singleton is closed in $W$. We will show that this same point is closed in $U$.

source.place: Tag 005E, lemma-quasi-compact-closed-point, and Tag 04ZA, lemma-Noetherian-quasi-compact; the choice used in the proof of Tag 02I7.

proof.text: Every prime of $A$ is contained in $\mathfrak m$: use [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] and uniqueness of the maximal ideal. In particular $V(\mathfrak m)=\{\mathfrak m\}$, so $U$ is open in $X$. Write $W=O\cap F$ with $O$ open and $F$ closed in $U$. Since $\{w\}$ is closed in $W$, write $\{w\}=W\cap C$ with $C$ closed in $U$. Hence $\{w\}=O\cap(F\cap C)$. The closed set $F\cap C$ contains the closure of $w$ in $U$, giving $\{w\}=O\cap\overline{\{w\}}^{\,U}$. Write $\mathfrak p$ for the prime of $w$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], this says $\{w\}=O\cap V(\mathfrak p)$, since $O\subseteq U$. As $U$ is open, $O$ is open in $X$; consequently $\{\mathfrak p\}$ is open in the whole subspace $V(\mathfrak p)$, not just in its puncture.

source.place: Tag 02IM, direct proof (1), the locally closed point becomes an open generic point of Spec(A/p); the subspace calculation is written out.

proof.text: Suppose $w$ were not closed in $U$. Its closure in $U$ is $V(\mathfrak p)\cap U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes], and contains a distinct point with prime $\mathfrak q$. Step 3 gives $\mathfrak p\subsetneq\mathfrak q\subsetneq\mathfrak m$. Put $B=A/\mathfrak p$. By [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure], $B$ is a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak p$. It is a domain: if $\bar a\bar b=0$, then $ab\in\mathfrak p$, so primality puts $a$ or $b$ in $\mathfrak p$. It is Noetherian directly from finite generation: for an ideal $J\subseteq B$, take finitely many generators of its inverse image in $A$ by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; their images generate $J$ because $A\to B$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 02IM, direct proof (1): passage to the Noetherian local domain A/p; quotient Noetherianity expanded as in Algebra lemma-Noetherian-permanence.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is homeomorphic to $V(\mathfrak p)$, with the zero prime mapping to $\mathfrak p$. The primes $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak m$ correspond to primes $\bar{\mathfrak q}$ and $\bar{\mathfrak m}$ with $(0)\subsetneq\bar{\mathfrak q}\subsetneq\bar{\mathfrak m}$: the inverse is the image under the quotient map and inverse image recovers the original prime. The closure and inclusion formula of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] gives the strict chain of irreducible closed sets $V(\bar{\mathfrak m})\subsetneq V(\bar{\mathfrak q})\subsetneq V(0)=\operatorname{Spec}B$. By the definition [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], $\dim\operatorname{Spec}B\geq2$. The homeomorphism and Step 3 also show that the singleton consisting of the zero prime is open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Tag 02IM, direct proof (1): the strict prime chain supplies dimension at least two, and the locally closed generic point supplies an open singleton.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-noetherian-local-domain-open-infinite] to $B$: Step 4 verified that it is a nonzero Noetherian local domain, and Step 5 verified dimension at least two. Its open singleton $\{(0)\}$ is nonempty and finite, contradicting that lemma. Thus the assumption of Step 4 was false: $\{w\}$ is closed in $U$, and $w\in W$ is the required point.

source.place: Tag 02IM, direct proof (1), final contradiction using Algebra Tag 02IG (lemma-Noetherian-local-domain-dim-2-infinite-opens).

proof_origin.place: Tag 02IM, lemma-complement-closed-point-Jacobson, direct proof of (1); expanded with the closed-point choice from Topology Tag 02I7 and 005E. Instead of introducing Jacobson terminology, choose a closed point in W and prove it is closed in the puncture by the same contradiction.
